svg.title: Building a faster Python re: no compatible replacement yet; Rust test runner failed twice; corrected follow-up is frozen, not run
svg.desc: The pinned Python 3.14.6 baseline was independently verified. The latest actual Rust replacement completed 13 workers, failed 928 compatibility checks and explicitly verified 8,965 passing observations; it is not compatible. The combined first-party buffer and match-serialization source belongs to the same Rust family. Its offline native build passed and recorded 28 successful compiler operations. The V8 and V9 test controllers both failed before starting any candidate. V9 left one empty recovery directory and thirteen synthetic error records, not real workers. A corrected V10 full-suite runner is source frozen and has not run. There are six replacement families, one actually tested family and zero currently runnable or qualified replacements. Speed, memory and repair effectiveness are not measured. The 31,237 original checks, 50 signature checks, 32 public observations and 32 large-input observations are separate. The 4,194,304-case final comparison has not been generated or opened. Historical Rust, C and Zig failures are preserved. Three and only three independently authenticated V10 source-only owners raise actual current lower bounds from 191 and 196 to 194 and 199; the small Rust failure receipt proves no failure-category breakdown.
svg.text: The goal: match Python exactly, then measure whether any from-scratch replacement is actually faster.
Rust was tested and is not compatible
13 real workers completed the frozen original comparison. Rust produced 928 differences and 8,965 explicitly verified passes.
A successful evidence receipt means the failure was saved; it does not mean the replacement passed.
Two Rust test runners failed; corrected follow-up frozen
The native build passed. V8 and V9 stopped before matching. V10 is source frozen, NOT RUN. Real new workers: 0.
Repair effectiveness, compatibility, speed and memory: NOT MEASURED.
Overall: how each replacement compares with Python
One row per existing family. A source idea, historical run or saved receipt is not a passing result.

The two genuine 2,147,483,648-byte Python tests have not been run by any replacement.
No historical result claims that the new source-only Rust idea has been tested.
Runtime independence: NOT ESTABLISHED. Speed, memory and uncertainty: NOT MEASURED.
Final comparison: all 4,194,304 hidden checks remain NOT GENERATED and NOT OPENED.
No candidate, compiler, native library, benchmark, clock or compressed evidence is run by this graph.
Corrected V10 full-suite test frozen; not yet run
Exactly three new V10 source files raise actual current lower bounds from 191 / 196 to 194 / 199.
The existing failure receipt does not prove a breakdown of individual failure categories.
